unresolvedQuestions: ROUTE TO core / src/core/Cinematic.js — SHOTS.valley. The terrain has the valley; the camera cannot see it. Ray-marching the centre ray: ground is 812.0 m out to 80 m, then 805.6 at 100, 779.7 at 130, 761.3 at 200, 691.8 at 300, 647.9 at 370, and 498.1 m ASL at its lowest inside 2 km — a 314 m drop. It crosses WATER_LEVEL 782 at 127 m along the ray. The drop is emphatically there. But from an eye 2.3 m above that floor the LAST VISIBLE GROUND is at 72 m and 811.9 m ASL, elevation angle -1.89 deg; all 1,928 sampled metres beyond it are occluded by the plateau lip, and the total visible drop is 0.1 m. ROUTE TO materials / src/render/Materials.js — the residual `detail` on the torii uprights. The vermilion recipe's decorative fields have these world scales at the pillar's UV density (uvScale 0.9, so the tile is 1.11 m, and the post resolves at 4.4 mm per drawing-buffer pixel): `sun` 2.2 cycles/tile = 50 cm, `chip` 4.2 = 26 cm, `dust` 5.5 = 20 cm, `grain` 56 in u = 2.0 cm (4.5 buffer px, amplitude only +/-9% of albedo via scalec), `micro` 128 = 8.7 mm, and the age-crazing net at 64x64 worley cells = 1.7 cm cells whose LINES are `1 - smoothstep(0, 0.040, f2-f1)` wide, i.e. about 0.3 texels of a 512 map — a fifth of a texel, so the craze net mips to its own mean before it ever reaches a fragment. Crazing is the one feature in that recipe with the hard high-contrast edge that mean |Laplacian| actually scores on (it is what the flagstone scores on: hard stone joints), and it is the only one that is invisible. Widening that smoothstep and raising the `mixc(s, PAL.vermAged, ... + crackLine*0.10)` weight is a Materials.js change worth one round. Measured support: detrended horizontal residual across the clean post face is 1.64-2.37 code RMS against 8.37-10.97 on the plaza in the same frame.

MECHANISM, measured: the pillar was `circleProfile(20)`, a perfect cylinder, and a perfect cylinder under one key has a strictly monotone Lambert ramp by construction — which is exactly the 204.6 195.9 187.3 174.7 163.2 152.2 142.7 133.6 124.1 115.4 104.4 96.9 92.8 87.5 82.8 77.3 74.2 76.9 sequence the critic quotes. FIX: adzedProfile(40, 9, 0.12), chosen by ablation against the real sweepProfile output and not by taste. Counting local minima of N.L on the lit arc under the shot's own sun, averaged over five rings: circle = 0.0 minima; 40 cols/9 lobes at depth 0.06 = 2.0, at 0.09 = 3.0, at 0.12 = 4.0 with a median dip of 19% of the local peak; the first guess (32 cols, 8 lobes, depth 0.028) scored 0.0, because a modulation smaller than the lattice's own per-column curvature step slows the ramp without ever reversing it. A 19% dip on this run's p50 range (204 down to 74) is 39 code at the lit end and 14 at the dark end. PREDICT: 4 or more local minima with dips of 14-39 code. Confidence high — it is geometry, not texture, and it was measured on the shipped mesh generator.

PREDICTION, torii uprights, criterion (a) — `detail` >= 6.5 in boxes 0.72,0.20,0.05,0.12 and 0.72,0.70,0.05,0.12, currently 1.48 and 1.88. PREDICT 3.5-4.8, A SHORTFALL, AND IT IS BEING REPORTED AS ONE BEFORE THE FACT. `detail` is a 1-pixel Laplacian and the review PNG is a 1.876x upscale, so nothing finer than about 2 review pixels can carry energy at all. Budgeting the three contributions this file can add: the nine adze facets are a ~70-review-px sinusoid, whose 1-px Laplacian is A*(2pi/P)^2 = about 0.15 mean, i.e. negligible to `detail` by construction (they are for criterion (b), not this one); the repaired grain streaks at 15 lines around the post are a ~22-review-px period at +/-11.5% vertex colour, about +0.6; the three shrinkage checks are hard 3-4 px dark lines with a lit lip and contribute about +0.5 each where one crosses the box. Sum 1.48 + ~2.2 = ~3.7. Reaching 6.5 needs high-contrast features at the 2-4 review-pixel scale and the only source of those on a lacquered post is the craze net, which is in Materials.js and is currently sub-texel (see unresolvedQuestions). Do not read a 3.7 as a failed fix; read it as the file's ceiling and route the rest.

MECHANISM DISCOVERED AND FIXED, torii uprights — axialGrain was aliasing, not grain-ing. It evaluated `noise.fbm2(cos(th)*9, sin(th)*9 + ...)` and `noise.noise2(cos(th)*27, sin(th)*27 + ...)`. Those are circles of radius 9 and 27 in noise space, arc lengths 56.5 and 170 noise units — and a 3-octave fbm's finest octave runs at 4x its base, so the two taps carried 226 and 170 features around a post the mesh samples at 20 columns. Both are an order of magnitude past the lattice Nyquist, so neither could draw a streak; they aliased to an uncorrelated value per column, which is the smooth blotchy mottle visible in `crop shots/phone-sun-r16.png 0.68,0.25,0.14,0.24`. The function's own comment ('20 around a 1.4 m circumference is a 7 cm line, about right for old cedar') states the intent exactly and the arithmetic never delivered it. Now parameterised: the field is evaluated on a circle of radius lines/2pi so its arc length is exactly `lines` noise periods, one streak per period, single-octave because an fbm's upper octaves are the part that cannot be sampled. Called with lines = 15 against a 20-line Nyquist at 40 columns.

PREDICTION, torii uprights, GUARDS. meanRGB must stay within +/-6% per channel of [158.6,97.7,55.8] and [123.5,69.8,37.9].
